result.topic_en: Calculations on the rational function y = η^3(η^4+7)/(7η^4+1) (connected with a symmetric subdivision of the sphere sketched in a figure), its derivative, the Laplace equation on the sphere in logarithmic/stereographic coordinates, and a symmetric expansion of a product in η and η'.
result.transcription:
$y = \eta^3 \frac{\eta^4+7}{7\eta^4+1}$
[figure: circle (sphere) divided by arcs into regions, points marked $i$, $\circ$, $\times$, $\infty$]
$y-1 = \frac{\eta^7+\beta\eta^3-\beta\eta^4-1}{\beta\eta^4+1}$
$7\eta^6+\beta 3\eta^2-4\beta\eta^3 \quad \beta=7$
$6\cdot7\eta^5+6\beta\eta^2-2\cdot6\beta\eta$
$y = \eta^3\frac{\eta^4+7}{7\eta^4+1}$
$\frac{\partial y}{\partial\eta}[?]$ $\quad \frac{\partial(\sin\theta\frac{\partial U}{\partial\theta})}{\sin\theta\partial\theta}+\frac{\partial^2U}{\sin\theta^2\partial\varphi^2}+\frac{\partial(rr\frac{\partial U}{\partial r})}{\partial r}$
$\sin\theta^2\left(\frac{\partial^2U}{\partial\log r^2}+\frac{\partial U}{\partial\log r}\right)+\frac{\partial^2U}{\partial(\log tg\frac{\theta}{2})^2}+\frac{\partial^2U}{\partial\varphi^2}=0$
$\frac{\partial U}{\partial\log\eta} \quad \log\eta=\log tg\frac{\theta}{2}+\varphi i \quad 2\varphi i=\log\eta-\log\eta'$
$\log\eta'=\log tg\frac{\theta}{2}-\varphi i \quad 2\log tg\frac{\theta}{2}=\log\eta+\log\eta'$
$=\frac12\frac{\partial U}{\partial\log tg\frac{\theta}{2}}-\frac12\frac{\partial U}{\partial\varphi}i$
$4\frac{\partial^2U}{\partial\log\eta\,\partial\log\eta'}+\frac{4\eta\eta'}{(1+\eta\eta')^2}\left(\frac{\partial^2U}{\partial\log r^2}+\frac{\partial U}{\partial\log r}\right)=0 \quad \frac{2tg\frac{\theta}{2}}{1+(tg\frac{\theta}{2})^2} \quad r\frac{1-\eta\eta'}{1+\eta\eta'} \quad r\frac{\eta}{1+\eta\eta'} \quad r\frac{\eta'}{1+\eta\eta'}$
$\partial y = \frac{\eta^7+7\eta^3}{7\eta^4+1}$
$\partial y = \frac{(7\eta^4+1)(7\eta^6+3\cdot7\eta^2)-(\eta^7+7\eta^3)4\cdot7\eta^3}{(7\eta^4+1)}\partial\eta$
$=7\eta^2\partial\eta\frac{(7\eta^4+1)(\eta^4+3)-(\eta^4+7)\cdot4\eta^4}{7\eta^4+1}$
$=7\eta^2\partial\eta\frac{3\eta^8-6\eta^4+3}{(7\eta^4+1)^2}=3\cdot7\cdot\eta^2\partial\eta\frac{(\eta^4-1)^2}{(7\eta^4+1)^2}$
$(7\eta'^4+1)(7\eta^4+1)(1+yy')=7\cdot7\eta^4\eta'^4+7(\eta^4+\eta'^4)+1+\eta^7\eta'^7+7\eta^3\eta'^3(\eta^4+\eta'^4)+7\cdot7\eta^3\eta'^3$
$=(\eta\eta'+1)$ [-$\eta\eta'^6+\ldots$-]
$=(\eta\eta'+1)\eta^3\eta'^3\left((\eta\eta')^3+\frac{1}{(\eta\eta')^3}-(\eta\eta')^2-\frac{1}{(\eta\eta')^2}+(\eta\eta'+\frac{1}{\eta\eta'})\left(1+7(\frac{\eta^2}{\eta'^2}+\frac{\eta'^2}{\eta^2})\right)+48-7(\frac{\eta}{\eta'})^2+(\frac{\eta'}{\eta})^2\right)$
$t^3-t^2+t\left(-2+7((\frac{\eta}{\eta'})^2+(\frac{\eta'}{\eta})^2)\right)+\left(1-7(\frac{\eta}{\eta'})^2\right)\left(1-7(\frac{\eta'}{\eta})^2\right)$

methods.what: Rational map of degree 7 with critical points determined by choosing β=7
Derivative of the rational map, showing branch points at η^4=1 and η=0
Laplace equation in spherical coordinates rewritten with log tan(θ/2) and φ
Stereographic complex coordinates η = tan(θ/2)e^{iφ}, η' conjugate
Laplace equation in coordinates log η, log η'
Expansion of (7η'^4+1)(7η^4+1)(1+yy') in symmetric form, reduced to a cubic in t
